evals.prompt: i need to wrap my chrome extension popup in ClerkProvider from @clerk/chrome-extension. what props does it need for redirect URLs to work inside a chrome extension?
evals.expected_output: ClerkProvider with publishableKey, redirect URLs using browser.runtime.getURL
expectations: Imports ClerkProvider from @clerk/chrome-extension (not @clerk/react or @clerk/nextjs)
Passes publishableKey prop to ClerkProvider
Uses browser.runtime.getURL (WXT) or chrome.runtime.getURL for redirect URL props (afterSignOutUrl, signInFallbackRedirectUrl, or similar)
Uses SignInButton or SignUpButton for unauthenticated state
Uses UserButton or user profile component for authenticated state

evals.prompt: my background service worker needs to make authenticated API calls to my server. how can it access the current user's session token?
evals.expected_output: Use createClerkClient from @clerk/chrome-extension/client with background: true to get a fresh session token
expectations: Imports createClerkClient from @clerk/chrome-extension/client (not @clerk/chrome-extension)
Calls createClerkClient with background: true option
Checks clerk.session before calling getToken()
Returns true from the runtime.onMessage listener to keep connection open for async sendResponse
Explains that background: true keeps the session fresh when popup is closed
Puts the listener inside defineBackground() in entrypoints/background.ts

evals.prompt: my content script needs to check if the user is signed in before injecting a UI overlay into the page. how do i access clerk auth state from a content script?
evals.expected_output: Content script uses message passing to background service worker which uses createClerkClient to get auth state
expectations: Explains that Clerk cannot be used directly in content scripts due to origin restrictions
Uses browser.runtime.sendMessage (or chrome.runtime.sendMessage) to request auth state from background service worker
Background script uses createClerkClient from @clerk/chrome-extension/client
Shows how to conditionally inject UI based on the response
Handles the async nature of message passing with return true in background listener
Defines the content script with defineContentScript({ matches, main }) in entrypoints/

evals.prompt: my chrome extension needs to let users sign in with google oauth. how do i set that up?
evals.expected_output: OAuth is not supported directly in popup or side panel -- must use syncHost to delegate to a web app
expectations: States clearly that OAuth is NOT supported in the popup or side panel
Explains that OAuth requires a redirect from the Identity Provider which Chrome extensions do not support
Introduces the syncHost approach to delegate auth to a companion web app
Mentions adding the WXT_CLERK_SYNC_HOST env var
Mentions adding syncHost prop to ClerkProvider

evals.prompt: i want my extension to automatically know when the user signs in on my web app without them having to interact with the popup. how?
evals.expected_output: Use syncHost prop + host_permissions + add extension ID to allowed_origins via Clerk API
expectations: Introduces the syncHost feature to sync auth state from web app to extension
Shows WXT_CLERK_SYNC_HOST env var setup for dev (.env.development) and prod (.env.production)
Shows adding syncHost prop to ClerkProvider
Shows host_permissions configuration in the wxt.config.ts manifest
Shows the curl command to add extension ID to allowed_origins via Clerk API

evals.prompt: every time i rebuild my chrome extension, the extension ID changes and clerk auth breaks because the redirect URLs don't match. how do i fix this?
evals.expected_output: Pin the extension ID by providing a consistent key in the manifest, then update Clerk Dashboard with the stable chrome-extension:// URL
expectations: Explains that the extension ID changes because Chrome derives it from the key field
Shows how to pin the extension ID by providing a consistent key via .env.chrome and the wxt.config.ts manifest
Mentions the WXT_CRX_PUBLIC_KEY env var and manifest key field
Mentions updating the Clerk Dashboard or allowed_origins with the stable chrome-extension:// URL
Shows the openssl commands to generate the key, public key, and CRX ID

evals.prompt: i'm migrating my clerk chrome extension from plasmo to wxt. what do i need to change?
evals.expected_output: Rename env vars to the WXT_ prefix, move the manifest from package.json to wxt.config.ts, move entrypoints, wrap the background in defineBackground, use browser.*, and reuse the existing public key
expectations: Renames PLASMO_PUBLIC_* env vars to WXT_* and reads them with import.meta.env
Moves the manifest config from package.json to wxt.config.ts using the function form manifest: () => ({ ... })
Moves the background to entrypoints/background.ts wrapped in defineBackground()
Uses browser.* instead of chrome.*
Reuses the existing public key as WXT_CRX_PUBLIC_KEY in .env.chrome so the CRX ID stays the same

evals.prompt: my chrome extension uses syncHost with my local web app. when i try to sign in to the extension i get 'Unable to authenticate this browser for your development instance'. how do i fix it?
evals.expected_output: Open the web app in the same browser first so the dev browser cookie exists; if it persists, clear localhost __clerk cookies and reload the web app
expectations: Explains that in development the extension uses the dev browser cookie the web app sets on localhost
Tells the user to open the web app (e.g. http://localhost:5173) in the same browser, then retry
Explains that cookies are shared across localhost ports, so another Clerk app can overwrite the cookie
Tells the user to delete __clerk/__client cookies for http://localhost in DevTools and reload the web app if the error persists
